name: OPA604 / OPA2604
tagline: Burr-Brown's early-90s ±24 V FET audio op-amp: the warm, tube-like (胆味) classic of CD players, sound cards, phones.

lineage.note: OPA2604 ©1991 (PDS-1069), OPA604 ©1992 (PDS-1161); Tucson, AZ. No second sources.
Renumbered SBOS006 (OPA2604) and SBOS019 (OPA604). OPA2604 EOL c. 2016; OPA604 still active.

part_numbers.note: 8-pin plastic mini-DIP, −25 to +85 °C. Sold on DIP adapters as OPA2604 substitute.
SO-8 and 2.5k reel; /2K5 status not individually confirmed. HeadAmp uses OPA604AU.
8-pin PDIP dual. Active in 2003/2015 addenda; lifetime buy by Aug 2016; no PDN.
SO-8 dual marked 'OPA 2604AU', MSL 3/260 °C; 2500 reel; in vivo Xplay 3S.
Green suffixes, CU NIPDAU finish; active in 2015 addendum, then family EOL.

key_specs.condition: G=1, 1 kHz, 3.5 Vrms, 1 kΩ, 80 kHz BW

key_specs.value: ±4.5 to ±24 V (±25 V abs max); late OPA2604 ±20 V
±10.5 mA typ, ±12 mA max (OPA2604, both amps)
±35 mA at ±12 V; Isc ±40 mA; ±12 V into 600 Ω
±1 mV typ, ±5 mV max; drift ±8 µV/°C
100 pA typ; offset current ±4 pA typ

reputation.summary: A defining 'Burr-Brown sound' part: warm, laid back, easy to listen to. Japanese bloggers call it 'the legendary op-amp' (伝説のオペアンプ); Soomal notes a strong valve flavour (胆味) and fame near the NE5532's, and found it in phones, DAPs and DACs including TempoTec Serenade. Its ±24 V rating suited high rails. 2025 Japanese tests reportedly rank it below MUSES8820/8920.
typical_uses: CD player and DAC I/V and output stages
DAC low-pass filters (Sony PHA-3, Shanling H3A, SoundAware)
Sound-card, USB DAC and headphone-amp rolling (reportedly Maverick D2)
Phone Hi-Fi paths (vivo Xplay/Xplay 3S, Smartisan T1)
Pro line stages on ±18 to ±24 V rails
caveats: Fast (20 MHz): one OPA2604AP oscillated above ~18 V in a Hansen-type amp; harder to use than OPA132/134.
Needs proper rails: Soomal found high distortion at ~±9.5 V (Teclast T51) and in the Smartisan T1.
Driving low-impedance headphones directly sounds thin and harsh (Soomal); Mineden reportedly finds the mids thin.
OPA2604 has been EOL since c. 2016; most market stock is fake.
Keep late or unknown OPA2604s at or below ±20 V: offset drift and rising Iq reported at ±24 V.

counterfeit_notes: Rampant: a 2019 survey found 70 of 75 Yahoo Auctions OPA2604s fake. Remarked TL072s show ~3 MHz, 13 V/µs (genuine: 20 MHz, 25 V/µs, ~10.5 mA); markings may wipe off. BB and TI logos are both genuine. Safest: two OPA604s.
alternatives: Two OPA604AP/AU on a dual adapter

silicon_changes.summary: Unannounced same-part-number derating: a TI non-conformance form said the OPA2604 must be held to ±20 V; at ±24 V parts showed long-term offset drift and higher Iq, likely thermal. TI E2E gives heat near ±24 V as the EOL reason. Datasheet SBOS006A (Dec 2015) still says ±24 V.
silicon_changes.identification: No marking, datasheet or PCN change; communicated by non-conformance form. Date codes unknown; late TI-logo lots suspect. OPA604 single reportedly unaffected.

spec_deltas.after: ±20 V (non-conformance constraint; never printed in a datasheet)

spec_deltas.before: Fully specified (PSRR spec covers ±5 to ±24 V)
spec_deltas.after: Reported long-term large offset drift and increased Iq

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Only ±20 to ±24 V designs risk offset drift and heat. Normal ±15 V rolling, distortion and noise are unaffected.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: designs relying on ±24 V may drift or run hot; ±15 V use unaffected.
silicon_changes.verification: diyAudio quotes the TI form; TI E2E cites heat near ±24 V. No PCN or die evidence.

silicon_changes.summary: OPA2604 discontinued ('OPA2604 has EOL status', TI E2E, by 2019–2020). In Aug 2016 it was nominally active but unobtainable (lead time over 6 months). TI suggested two OPA604s, OPA2134 or OPA1656; diyAudio cites OPA1688. No dual high-voltage JFET audio drop-in remains for ±20 V+ rails.
silicon_changes.identification: Lifecycle only. DigiKey lists OPA2604AU/2K5 obsolete; OPA2604AP widely listed obsolete. TI published no PCN/PDN. OPA604 remains active.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None to the silicon. Current stock is old or remarked; suggested replacements are different dies.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: dual no longer made; OPA604 needs a two-package adapter; OPA2134/OPA1656 not rated for ±20 V+.
silicon_changes.verification: TI E2E engineer confirms EOL, OPA604 active; exact EOL date uncertain without a PDN.

revision_history.changes: OPA604 Burr-Brown datasheet (©1992, printed May 1995). Earlier letters and their changes not found.
OPA604 TI re-issue ('January 1992 – revised September 2003'); current on ti.com. Changes not captured; fits TI's 2003 addenda.
OPA2604 (©1991): distortion-rejection block diagram (patents 5053718, 5019789), copper-leadframe note, θJA 90 °C/W. Earlier letters not found.
PDS-1069E body stamped SBOS006 with 3-Oct-2003 addendum (AP, AU, AU/2K5 active). No content changes.
TI template; ESD, layout, application sections; per-package θJA (SOIC 107.9, PDIP 46.7 °C/W); ±4.5–±24 V, −40–100 °C. Electrical table unchanged.

revision_chains.note: PDS-1069A to PDS-1069D (from c. 1991) not found; rtellason and datasheet4u copies are candidates.
Original dated January 1992; PDS-1161B and earlier missing; PDS-1161D unknown.
Unlettered c. 2000 TI re-issue not found; Rev. A still current.

open_questions: OPA2604 EOL: PDN/PCN number and last-time-buy dates (TI E2E 953479 asks for the AU/2K5 PCN).
±20 V derating: original TI document, affected date codes, and whether OPA604 singles share the issue.
Missing Burr-Brown letters: OPA2604 PDS-1069 to PDS-1069D; OPA604 PDS-1161 to PDS-1161B; unlettered SBOS019.
Capture the OPA604 SBOS019A electrical table and compare with PDS-1161C; which mirrors hold which edition?
Is the DiyEden-translated survey Tangent's 'Notes on Audio Op-Amps'? Where did the OPA1688 suggestion originate?

claims_confirmed: OPA2604 discontinued; heat near ±24 V cited; OPA1642 or OPA2156 suggested (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/766644/opa2604-eol).
OPA2604 no longer available from TI or distributors; EOL never announced (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/793405/opa2604-eol).
diyAudio (2016-08-24): OPA2604 must be held to ±20 V; offset drift, higher Iq at ±24 V; lifetime buy (https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/opa2604-is-dead.295854/).
TI E2E thread asks for OPA2604AU/2K5 status and PCN (https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/953479/status-of-the-opa2604au-2k5-pcn-available).
TI FAQ presents OPA1656 as OPA2134/OPA2604 replacement (https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/911603/faq-opa1656-next-generation-opa2134-and-opa2604-replacement).
OPA604 active on ti.com; datasheet Rev. A; AP/AU orderable (https://www.ti.com/product/OPA604).
SBOS019A: January 1992, revised September 2003; PDS-1161C May 1995; mini-DIP and SO-8, −25 to +85 °C (https://www.hifituning24.de/downloads/opa604.pdf).
TI gpn link resolves to the OPA604 datasheet (https://www.ti.com/lit/gpn/OPA604).
Survey of 75 Yahoo Auctions OPA2604s found 70 fakes (fakecomponents, 2019-09-19) (https://nw-electric.way-nifty.com/blog/2019/10/post-19bc00.html).
'伝説のオペアンプ BB OPA2604' label confirmed (http://www.southenst.com/cgi-bin/blog/html/art/00174.html).
PDS-1069E / Oct 1997 / SBOS006 copies at hirokun.jp, media.digikey, Octopart (https://hirokun.jp/OPA2604.pdf).
DigiKey hosts a TI-template OPA2604 PDF (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/842/OPA2604.pdf).
Audiokarma 'OPA2604AP (obsolete)' and GroupDIY substitution threads exist (https://audiokarma.org/forums/threads/op-amp-upgrades-opa2604ap-obsolete.935775/).
refuted_claims: 'TI discontinued the OPA2604AP around 2019': diyAudio reported a lifetime buy already in Aug 2016; 2019 threads only confirm it was gone.
'Only the DIP was discontinued': the whole OPA2604 family is EOL; TI's heat reason is not DIP-specific. AU and AU/2K5 set obsolete.
'new_western_elec found 70 of 75 fakes': the survey was by fakecomponents (2019-09-19); new_western_elec only reported it.
